A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MCNC and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. All supplied material supports comparison, including v2 Appendices A.1–A.6; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments, LLaMA fine-tuning and throughput measurements, and generator-design ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and LLaMA experiments, plus MNIST ablations, random-versus-trained generator comparisons, and CPU-to-GPU transfer measurements.

M1.justification: v1 trains the generator with SWGAN before freezing it; v2 uses a frozen, randomly initialized sinusoidal generator for its main method. Sections 3.2–3.3 replace the configurable m-component sum with one amplitude/input pair per chunk and use residual optimization around fixed initial weights for training from scratch. Residual adaptation for PEFT already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST digit classification for generator-design experiments. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100, Alpaca, and MMLU remain covered. The added ViT-S architecture expands model configurations within existing ImageNet-100 coverage.

E2.justification: The ImageNet transformer comparison switches from LoRA to Magnitude and PLATON pruning, while LLaMA Table 4 adds rank-one LoRA alongside NOLA. Standalone LoRA disappears from the ResNet-18 comparison. DPF and SuRP disappear specifically from ResNet-20/CIFAR-10, although retained in other CIFAR comparisons. Appendix A.4 also introduces a sparse linear-classifier comparison on MNIST.

E3.justification: The reported LLaMA-7B adapter rank changes from 16 to 8, and MCNC's learning rate changes from 0.05 to 0.01. ResNet learning rates, plateau patience, and compression budgets also change. New ViT pruning and MNIST experiments introduce additional training and evaluation protocols. CIFAR pruning counts lose v1's ×2 storage factor, while ViT storage accounting assumes half-precision indices. These reported revisions do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the ablations: frequency and fixed-compression k/d studies move to MNIST with revised settings, and new analyses test activation functions, target-model size, generator initialization, width, depth, and residual connections. Random-versus-trained CIFAR controls and a transfer-speed experiment are added. v1's explicit m>1 ablation and CIFAR compression-accuracy curve are absent.

E5.justification: v1 reports ± accuracies without specifying repeat counts. v2 Appendix A.4 specifies three-trial averages for its ablations, and Section 4.3 specifies 100 transfer-timing repetitions. Many tables retain ± reporting, while the new ViT pruning table gives point estimates. There is no evidence of increased run counts for retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive ViT, MNIST, and transfer-timing results and revises existing metrics. CIFAR-100/ResNet-20 accuracy with MCNC plus LoRA changes from 39.52 to 36.7; Table 4 changes MCNC's LLaMA-7B throughput from 3.2 to 6.2 samples/s and reconstruction cost from 2.75 to 1.37 GFLOPs. Generator, rank, and other settings change, preventing controlled performance-gain claims. v1's no-LoRA CIFAR accuracies remain, rounded, as trained-generator controls in v2 Table 9.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 and Figure 2 introduce an explicit Wasserstein-based uniformity score. Appendix A.6 adds a derivation of reconstruction operation counts from layer dimensions, adapter ranks, and generator chunk counts; v1 reports FLOP totals without this derivation. Neither version supplies formal performance guarantees.

C1.justification: The introduction reframes the methodological contribution around an untrained random sinusoidal generator, replacing v1's emphasis on learning the generator and its separate generative-modeling contribution. v2 also explicitly foregrounds reduced CPU-to-GPU loading time. The broader claims of nonlinear compression and effectiveness across vision and language remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets generator training as offering only marginal gains and favors random generators for scalability and seed-based storage. It adds explanations involving activation choice, target-model overparameterization, and initialization-frequency interactions. Appendix A.5 attributes poor low-k performance to amplitude parameters consuming more of the budget, whereas v1 emphasized optimization and coverage difficulties. The concluding limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, a PyTorch layer example, generator defaults, detailed training and pruning settings, per-compression augmentation choices, convolutional LoRA reshaping instructions, and reconstruction-cost accounting in Appendices A.1–A.6. This substantially expands v1's limited implementation documentation. The example nevertheless contains an undefined n_alpha variable, limiting its executability as printed.

R1.justification: v2 expands pruning and hashing context with PLATON, structured pruning, and structured multi-hashing, and adds supporting implementation references. MIRACLE, generalized sliced Wasserstein, and Fourier-feature references disappear. The central positioning as a nonlinear extension/generalization of PRANC and NOLA remains, making this a focused literature and positioning revision.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work paragraphs are extensively rewritten, Section 3.1 gains a reorganized explanatory structure, and image experiments are grouped and reordered to lead with ImageNet transformers. The ablation narrative is substantially rewritten and technical material is organized into six appendix subsections. The title, author ordering, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn around the random generator and chunkwise residual reconstruction. Figure 2 replaces five sphere illustrations with an activation-by-frequency grid carrying quantitative coverage annotations; v1 Figure 3 disappears. Comparison tables gain substantially different structures, including model-size percentages and reference columns, alongside new ablation tables, hyperparameter tables, and a formatted code listing.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens design validation and reproducibility: Table 9 directly tests the need for generator training, the expanded ablations examine previously underexplored choices, and Appendices A.2–A.6 document settings and reconstruction costs. New pruning and rank-one LoRA comparisons improve empirical context. Benefits are tempered by removed analyses, the undefined variable in Appendix A.1, and Section 4.1 pruning commentary that conflicts with Table 1. The substantial gains in methodological support and documentation outweigh these localized defects.
